$M_T(\lambda)\otimes_T\kappa(p)$ is the Verma module over $\kappa(p)$ with
highest weight $\lambda+\epsilon_p$ for $\mathfrak g\otimes_{\mathbb C}\kappa(p)$.
For a complex-valued point $\epsilon:T\to\mathbb C$, this is precisely
$-\otimes_T\mathbb C_\epsilon$ and the ordinary complex Verma module
$M(\lambda+\epsilon)$. An arbitrary localization can have closed points
whose residue fields are larger than $\mathbb C$; for example,
$T=\mathbb C(t)$ has only the residue field $\mathbb C(t)$ and has no
complex-valued point. By the tensor identity for finite-dimensional modules
and the Verma flags of tensor products
([[lem-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-verma-flags]]) the
specializations have Verma constituents over their residue fields of highest
weights $\lambda+\nu+\epsilon_p$, where $\nu$ runs through the weights of the
finite-dimensional tensor factors. At complex-valued points they can meet several
central-character blocks, whose labels are the dot-Weyl orbits through these
highest weights ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]); a generic
parameter is generally nonintegral, and the distinct constituent labels have distinct central characters at the
generic parameter: an equality $\lambda+\gamma+\tau+\rho=w(\lambda+\gamma'+\tau+\rho)$
as affine functions of $\tau$ forces $w=1$ by comparing linear parts,
and then $\gamma=\gamma'$ ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]).

boundaries explicitly: $\pi_\alpha$ is exact, being Hom from a projective
object; its left adjoint is right exact but not exact in general; it sends

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). In a finite
highest-weight block or in a lower Serre ideal $\Gamma$ of
[[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]]
put
$$T_\Gamma=\bigoplus_{A\in\Gamma}T(A),\qquad R_\Gamma=\operatorname{End}(T_\Gamma)^{\mathrm{op}},$$
the **characteristic tilting generator** and its opposite endomorphism ring.
By the classification theorem
([[thm-indecomposable-tiltings-exist-and-are-classified-in-parabolic-category-o]])
$T_\Gamma$ is Ext-self-orthogonal and has finite projective dimension.

The **Ringel-dual category** of $\Gamma$ is the category of finite-dimensional
left $R_\Gamma$-modules, made a highest-weight category by the reversed poset
and the standards
$$\Delta_R(A)=\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,\nabla(A)),\qquad A\in\Gamma .$$
The functor $\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,-)$ is exact and fully faithful on
costandard-filtered objects and identifies them with standard-filtered
Ringel-dual objects; projectives of the dual category correspond to tilting
objects of the original. Its algebraic realization by the opposite-parabolic
highest-weight quotient is proved in the next theorem.

cited_passages: **Given:** A finite highest-weight block or lower Serre ideal $\Gamma$ with its generalized standards $M(A)$, costandards $\nabla(A)$, tiltings $T(A)$ and filtered categories, as in [[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]] and [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].

the **characteristic tilting generator** and its opposite endomorphism ring.
By the classification theorem
([[thm-indecomposable-tiltings-exist-and-are-classified-in-parabolic-category-o]])
$T_\Gamma$ is Ext-self-orthogonal and has finite projective dimension.

**Given:** A finite highest-weight block or lower Serre ideal $\Gamma$ with its generalized standards $M(A)$, costandards $\nabla(A)$, tiltings $T(A)$ and filtered categories, as in [[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]] and [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].

[F1] Tilting and filtered structure ([[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]], [[thm-indecomposable-tiltings-exist-and-are-classified-in-parabolic-category-o]]): the homological criteria, the maximal-support normalization of the indecomposable tiltings $T(A)$, that every tilting is a finite sum of these, and closedness of the flag categories under extensions and summands.
proof_uses: 1.1 **Ext-self-orthogonality and finite projective dimension.** Each $T(A)$ has a standard flag and each $T(B)$ has a costandard flag. All positive $\operatorname{Ext}$ groups between these two kinds of flags vanish by the locally proved criterion of [F1], giving $\operatorname{Ext}^i(T(A),T(B))=0$ for every $i>0$. The actual projective sequence onto each standard has a standard-filtered kernel with strictly higher labels; starting at maximal labels, where the standard is projective, downward induction on the finite poset gives finite projective dimension for every standard. Long exact sequences along a finite standard flag then give finite projective dimension for every $T(A)$ and their finite sum $T_\Gamma$. The second flag in the Ext argument is costandard, and no standard/standard Ext vanishing is assumed. [F1, F2, F3]

2.1 **Costandard presentations by tiltings.** Dual to the normalized standard inclusion $M(A)\hookrightarrow T(A)$, every costandard object admits a surjection from a tilting object with costandard-filtered kernel; induction on the costandard flag length gives such presentations for every costandard-filtered object. [F1, step 1.1]

3.1 **Exactness and full faithfulness of $\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,-)$.** On costandard flags the functor sends the presentations of step 2.1 to projective presentations of the images; two tilting presentations lift every map and identify its kernel, so the functor is exact on costandard-filtered objects and fully faithful. It sends tilting objects to projective objects because $\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,T(A))$ is a direct summand of the regular module. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 **The highest-weight structure of the dual.** The quotient $\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,T(A))\to\Delta_R(A)=\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,\nabla(A))$ has a kernel filtered by standards with labels strictly higher in the reversed order, and its endomorphism ring is $\mathbb C$ with head labelled $A$; this follows from full faithfulness in step 3.1 and the maximal tilting support of [F1]. Hence the Ringel-dual category is highest weight with the reversed poset and the displayed standards, and its filtered image is $\mathcal F(\Delta_R)$, not $\mathcal F(\nabla_R)$. [F1, step 3.1]

rows.consumer_statement_or_definition:
Work over $\mathbb C$ and assume the Axiom of Choice where projective covers,
duality and locally unital assemblies enter. Let
$\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ be a pyramid with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, let $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ be admissible in the sense that
$c_i-c_j\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_i=c_j$, and let
$\mathcal O_c^d$ be the relevant summand of the genuine parabolic
category $\mathcal O$ attached to the labels $c$ and the degree $d$: its
objects are the modules whose column-strict labels have nonnegative integral
differences from the ground entries of each column, i.e. the labels with
$\Lambda$-diagram content $c_j+q_j-n$ in the sense of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] (the ambient categories are the
ones of [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]
and [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]).

For a $U(\mathfrak m)$-finitely-generated object $N$ of genuine parabolic
$\mathcal O$, the **Whittaker functor** is the covariant finite-dimensional dual
$$V(N):=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak m}(N,\mathbb C_\chi)^*.$$
Its $W(\lambda)$ action is obtained from the continuous $\chi$-part of the right
linear dual, then the reflected head/tail identification proved below. In the
notation $D_{\mathrm{row}}\mathrm{Wh}D_{\mathrm{row}}$, the middle Whittaker
operation is performed on this continuous $\chi$-part, not on the uncompleted
ordinary row-restricted dual. Write $N(A)$ for source standard objects,
$L_{\mathcal O}(A)$ for source simples, and $L_W(A)$ for the resulting
nonzero simple $W$-modules. These namespaces are distinct.

The verification below records the properties used on this page: $V$ is exact
on the $U(\mathfrak m)$-finitely-generated objects of genuine parabolic
$\mathcal O$ and intertwines tensoring with finite-dimensional
Cartan-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-modules, the Casimir and the flips; $V$
is distinct from the Hecke quotient $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$
constructed later; for the ground simple projective-injective $P_c$ and
$T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ one has $V(P_c)=\mathbb C_c$ and
$V(T)=V_c^{\otimes d}$; and $V(L_{\mathcal O}(A))$ is the simple $W$-module $L_W(A)$ for
standard labels $A$ and zero otherwise. Nonintegral origins use the typed
equivalence of the all-weight Harish-Chandra comparison of the source; no
arbitrary complex $c$ is identified with an integral block. After fixing the
ground identification $i_0\colon V(P_c)\to\mathbb C_c$, the compatible functor
and the maps $j_d$ are unique up to the normalized unique natural isomorphism;
without this normalization scalar automorphisms prevent literal uniqueness.

cited_passages: [F7] The normalized highest-component projection is an actual module map with saturated integral kernel spanned exactly by off-standard source dual-canonical $L_A$ and independent image basis $D_A$; the original-order source upper ground component is exactly $\mathrm{Std}$ ([[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]]). The standard/simple matrix is the genuine parabolic composition matrix and gives the simple-class dictionary by inversion ([[thm-parabolic-kl-polynomials-give-the-dual-canonical-transition-matrix]], [[thm-the-parabolic-o-grothendieck-group-is-the-integral-fock-module]]). Exact biadjoint residue functors have the valid-entry standard flags, the corresponding Chevalley action, and the actual simple-head/socle theorem ([[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]], [[lem-the-local-affine-hecke-socle-argument-for-residue-translations]]). proof_uses: 1.20 The actual highest-component projection $\pi$ is module-linear and, in its integral $L/D$ bases, is the coordinate projection with $\pi L_A=0$ off $\mathrm{Std}$ and $\pi L_A=D_A$ on $\mathrm{Std}$. Its kernel is therefore a direct summand, and specialization at parameter one gives exactly $K=\bigoplus_{A\notin\mathrm{Std}}\mathbb Z L_A(1)$, with no extra specialization kernel. For a nonstandard simple, exact residue translation and the source $K_0$ dictionary give $[f_iL_O(A)]\in K$ and $[e_iL_O(A)]\in K$. Expanding these actual modules in their simple classes and projecting gives a sum of independent $D_B(1)$ with nonnegative composition multiplicities; each standard-label coefficient must vanish. Exactness then proves that the Serre subcategory of objects with only off-standard composition factors is stable under both residue functors. In several complex cosets apply the product of component coordinate projections and the typed residue shift $i^{\mathrm{int}}=i-c_\kappa+n-n_\kappa$. To treat finitely many objects or elementary moves outside an initial admitted cut, shift every origin down by a sufficiently large common integer; the category, cosets and standard predicate are unchanged and all those labels lie above the new ground. No order on different complex cosets is used. [F1, F4, F7, construct, algebra]

1.21 Every standard $N(C)$ embeds in an iterated lowering translate of a standard simple. To construct the monomorphism, shift the entries of column $j$ upwards by an integer $k_j\ge0$, choosing these successively so that every shifted entry in that column is greater than every earlier-column entry in the same coset. The resulting $B$ is standard and minimal in its fixed-multiset Bruhat orbit; the triangular standard/simple multiplicity matrix gives $N(B)=L_O(B)$. For each column $j=2,\ldots,l$, list its original entries increasingly and lower its smallest entry from $a+k_j$ to $a$, then its next entry, and so on, using $e_{a+k_j-1},\ldots,e_a$ in that chronological order. At each step the distinguished change in column $j$ is valid: its smaller entries already have their original values, while its larger entries and the later columns remain above the required range. Every other valid change occurs in an earlier column and gives a strictly smaller label in the prefix Bruhat order. The distinguished standard is therefore the largest section of the multiplicity-free residue standard flag. Move it to the bottom by splitting adjacent extensions. Indeed the projective-cover kernel of $N(D)$ is filtered by standards $N(E)$ with $E>D$, while $\operatorname{Hom}(N(E),N(C))=0$ unless $E\le C$, since a nonzero image has its $L_O(E)$ head as a composition factor of $N(C)$. Thus for largest $D$ and smaller $C$, every map from that projective kernel to $N(C)$ vanishes; the projective-cover exact sequence gives $\operatorname{Ext}^1(N(D),N(C))=0$. This proves the precise splitting orientation locally from the highest-weight suppliers. This produces an actual monomorphism at each elementary step. Exactness preserves these monomorphisms under the remaining lowering functors, giving $N(C)\hookrightarrow e_{i_1}\cdots e_{i_r}L_O(B)$. For mixed cosets the same construction is performed only among comparable entries; the typed standard and tensor equivalence transports the inclusion. [F1, F4, F7, construct, algebra]

2.4 If a simple $L_O(A)$ embeds in $N(C)$, compose with the monomorphism of step 1.21 and use repeated biadjunction to obtain a nonzero, hence surjective, map $f_{i_r}\cdots f_{i_1}L_O(A)\to L_O(B)$ with $B$ standard. Step 1.20 excludes this when $A$ is nonstandard. Thus the socle of every standard has only standard labels. For a simple submodule of a standard-filtered module, choose the first filtration term it intersects nontrivially: it lies in that term, has zero intersection with the preceding term and embeds in the corresponding standard section. Consequently EVERY standard-filtered module has standard-label socle, including all projectives and the tensor object $T$. This is a statement about actual submodules, not about its entire list of composition factors. [F1, F7, step 1.20, step 1.21, construct, algebra]

3.3 The ground central-character multiset determines a unique column-strict label. Within each charge coset its smallest entry $c_\kappa+1-n$ occurs once per column; strictness permits that entry at most once in each column and only at its bottom, so its multiplicity forces every such bottom entry. Remove these entries and repeat with the next minimum in every remaining column. Induction fixes all ground entries. Different charge cosets are distinct and are never compared. In the source convention $\lambda_i=a_i+i-1$, the coordinates $\lambda_i+\rho_i=a_i+(N-1)/2$ show that the central character is precisely this entry multiset. Hence the ground block has the sole column-strict label $A_c$. The generalized standard has diagonal simple multiplicity one and no other simple label in this block, so $N(A_c)=L_O(A_c)$. Therefore the projective summands of $T_d$ are exactly the covers of the standard-label simples, with positive multiplicities; they are injective as summands of $T_d$. It follows that every nonzero submodule $X\subseteq T_d$ has a nonzero standard-label simple socle. Exact $V$ and the nonvanishing already proved in step 1.18 then give $V(X)\ne0$. This proves the required detector; it does not assert that every composition factor of $T_d$ is standard or that $T_d$ generates the whole parabolic category. [F1, F4, F7, step 1.18, step 2.4, construct, algebra]

8.2 $V$ maps $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}$ into $\operatorname{End}_{W}(M)^{\mathrm{op}}=B$ by step 2.5, and its image contains $B$ because every target Hecke operator is the transport of its actual source Casimir/place operator. A nonzero source endomorphism has a nonzero image $X\subseteq T$. Step 3.3 proves $V(X)\ne0$, and exactness identifies $V(X)$ with the image of its transported endomorphism. Hence the endomorphism map is injective as well as surjective, giving $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}=B$. 9.1 Choose a full finite projective generator Q of the genuine O summand containing T as an explicit summand and write its algebra as A; the projector onto T is e and B=eAe. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F7, step 1.18, step 3.3, step 8.2, construct, algebra]

proof_uses: 1.1 Let U=U(m), I=I_chi. Replace x by y=x−chi(x). These shifted generators have the original brackets, because chi vanishes on brackets. Choose a basis adapted to the lower-central filtration, with weight w_i the largest lower-central index containing its basis vector. PBW reordering and the commutator formula show that I^n is spanned by ordered monomials of total lower-central weight≥n: one inclusion follows from reordering n factors, while the reverse follows because each basis vector of weight w lies in I^w, being a linear combination of iterated brackets of length w. [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

1.2 The Rees algebra R=⊕_(n≥0) I^n t^n is generated by y_i t^r, 0≤r≤w_i. Their span is a finite-dimensional Lie algebra: a nonzero bracket component y_k has w_k≥w_i+w_j, so r+s≤w_k. PBW gives its enveloping algebra a polynomial associated graded. For any left ideal, Hilbert basis gives finitely many generators of its homogeneous leading ideal; lift them and subtract matching highest-degree terms until the nonnegative degree decreases to zero. The lifts generate the original ideal. Thus the enveloping algebra is left noetherian, and its surjection onto R makes R left noetherian. For a left ideal J⊂U, ⊕(J∩I^n)t^n is a graded left ideal of R and has finitely many homogeneous generators. For fixed k, choosing n greater than k plus their largest degrees gives J∩I^n⊂I^k J. This is the precise Artin–Rees consequence needed here. [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

1.3 Set E_chi=∪_(n≥0)(U/I^n)^*, with left action (x f)(r)=f(r x). To prove injectivity, take a U-linear map phi:J→E_chi. U is noetherian, so choose finitely many generators of J. A common I^k kills their images and hence all images, since I is two-sided. The scalar functional lambda(j)=phi(j)(1) kills I^k J. Choose n with J∩I^n⊂I^k J, extend lambda from J/(J∩I^n) to U/I^n, and call the extension a∈E_chi. The map U→E_chi, u↦u a, extends phi, because at r its value on j is a(rj)=phi(rj)(1)=phi(j)(r). Baer's criterion gives injectivity. This supplies the injective-continuous-dual assertion cited without proof in BK Lemma8.20. [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

1.4 For a U(m)-finitely generated g-module X, evaluation at1 identifies Hom_m(X,E_chi) with the scalar functionals lambda:X→C that kill I^n X for some n. Indeed, reconstruct the map by F_lambda(v)(r)=lambda(rv); finitely many generators give a common n. The right U(g)-action is (lambda·u)(v)=lambda(uv). On E-valued maps its formula is therefore [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]
1.5 (F·u)(v)(r)=lambda(u r v), [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

1.7 The right action preserves continuity. For a fixed u∈U(g), the finite PBW subspace generated by all iterated ad m on u is finite-dimensional and its negative-column action is nilpotent; sufficiently long products of ad m vanish. proof_uses: 1.1 Let U=U(m), I=I_chi. Replace x by y=x−chi(x). These shifted generators have the original brackets, because chi vanishes on brackets. Choose a basis adapted to the lower-central filtration, with weight w_i the largest lower-central index containing its basis vector. PBW reordering and the commutator formula show that I^n is spanned by ordered monomials of total lower-central weight≥n: one inclusion follows from reordering n factors, while the reverse follows because each basis vector of weight w lies in I^w, being a linear combination of iterated brackets of length w. [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

1.2 The Rees algebra R=⊕_(n≥0) I^n t^n is generated by y_i t^r, 0≤r≤w_i. Their span is a finite-dimensional Lie algebra: a nonzero bracket component y_k has w_k≥w_i+w_j, so r+s≤w_k. PBW gives its enveloping algebra a polynomial associated graded. For any left ideal, Hilbert basis gives finitely many generators of its homogeneous leading ideal; lift them and subtract matching highest-degree terms until the nonnegative degree decreases to zero. The lifts generate the original ideal. Thus the enveloping algebra is left noetherian, and its surjection onto R makes R left noetherian. For a left ideal J⊂U, ⊕(J∩I^n)t^n is a graded left ideal of R and has finitely many homogeneous generators. For fixed k, choosing n greater than k plus their largest degrees gives J∩I^n⊂I^k J. This is the precise Artin–Rees consequence needed here. [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

1.3 Set E_chi=∪_(n≥0)(U/I^n)^*, with left action (x f)(r)=f(r x). To prove injectivity, take a U-linear map phi:J→E_chi. U is noetherian, so choose finitely many generators of J. A common I^k kills their images and hence all images, since I is two-sided. The scalar functional lambda(j)=phi(j)(1) kills I^k J. Choose n with J∩I^n⊂I^k J, extend lambda from J/(J∩I^n) to U/I^n, and call the extension a∈E_chi. The map U→E_chi, u↦u a, extends phi, because at r its value on j is a(rj)=phi(rj)(1)=phi(j)(r). Baer's criterion gives injectivity. This supplies the injective-continuous-dual assertion cited without proof in BK Lemma8.20. [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

1.4 For a U(m)-finitely generated g-module X, evaluation at1 identifies Hom_m(X,E_chi) with the scalar functionals lambda:X→C that kill I^n X for some n. Indeed, reconstruct the map by F_lambda(v)(r)=lambda(rv); finitely many generators give a common n. The right U(g)-action is (lambda·u)(v)=lambda(uv). On E-valued maps its formula is therefore [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

1.7 The right action preserves continuity. For a fixed u∈U(g), the finite PBW subspace generated by all iterated ad m on u is finite-dimensional and its negative-column action is nilpotent; sufficiently long products of ad m vanish. On this continuous-dual module the right shifted m-action is locally nilpotent. Injectivity of E_chi makes Hom_m(−,E_chi) exact, and right Skryabin makes its Whittaker vectors exact. These Whittaker vectors are precisely Hom_m(X,C_chi). Dualizing this finite-dimensional vector space gives an exact covariant functor. [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

proof_uses: 1.20 The actual highest-component projection $\pi$ is module-linear and, in its integral $L/D$ bases, is the coordinate projection with $\pi L_A=0$ off $\mathrm{Std}$ and $\pi L_A=D_A$ on $\mathrm{Std}$. Its kernel is therefore a direct summand, and specialization at parameter one gives exactly $K=\bigoplus_{A\notin\mathrm{Std}}\mathbb Z L_A(1)$, with no extra specialization kernel. For a nonstandard simple, exact residue translation and the source $K_0$ dictionary give $[f_iL_O(A)]\in K$ and $[e_iL_O(A)]\in K$. Expanding these actual modules in their simple classes and projecting gives a sum of independent $D_B(1)$ with nonnegative composition multiplicities; each standard-label coefficient must vanish. Exactness then proves that the Serre subcategory of objects with only off-standard composition factors is stable under both residue functors. In several complex cosets apply the product of component coordinate projections and the typed residue shift $i^{\mathrm{int}}=i-c_\kappa+n-n_\kappa$. To treat finitely many objects or elementary moves outside an initial admitted cut, shift every origin down by a sufficiently large common integer; the category, cosets and standard predicate are unchanged and all those labels lie above the new ground. No order on different complex cosets is used. [F1, F4, F7, construct, algebra]

1.21 Every standard $N(C)$ embeds in an iterated lowering translate of a standard simple. To construct the monomorphism, shift the entries of column $j$ upwards by an integer $k_j\ge0$, choosing these successively so that every shifted entry in that column is greater than every earlier-column entry in the same coset. The resulting $B$ is standard and minimal in its fixed-multiset Bruhat orbit; the triangular standard/simple multiplicity matrix gives $N(B)=L_O(B)$. For each column $j=2,\ldots,l$, list its original entries increasingly and lower its smallest entry from $a+k_j$ to $a$, then its next entry, and so on, using $e_{a+k_j-1},\ldots,e_a$ in that chronological order. At each step the distinguished change in column $j$ is valid: its smaller entries already have their original values, while its larger entries and the later columns remain above the required range. Every other valid change occurs in an earlier column and gives a strictly smaller label in the prefix Bruhat order. The distinguished standard is therefore the largest section of the multiplicity-free residue standard flag. Move it to the bottom by splitting adjacent extensions. Indeed the projective-cover kernel of $N(D)$ is filtered by standards $N(E)$ with $E>D$, while $\operatorname{Hom}(N(E),N(C))=0$ unless $E\le C$, since a nonzero image has its $L_O(E)$ head as a composition factor of $N(C)$. Thus for largest $D$ and smaller $C$, every map from that projective kernel to $N(C)$ vanishes; the projective-cover exact sequence gives $\operatorname{Ext}^1(N(D),N(C))=0$. This proves the precise splitting orientation locally from the highest-weight suppliers. This produces an actual monomorphism at each elementary step. Exactness preserves these monomorphisms under the remaining lowering functors, giving $N(C)\hookrightarrow e_{i_1}\cdots e_{i_r}L_O(B)$. For mixed cosets the same construction is performed only among comparable entries; the typed standard and tensor equivalence transports the inclusion. [F1, F4, F7, construct, algebra]

2.4 If a simple $L_O(A)$ embeds in $N(C)$, compose with the monomorphism of step 1.21 and use repeated biadjunction to obtain a nonzero, hence surjective, map $f_{i_r}\cdots f_{i_1}L_O(A)\to L_O(B)$ with $B$ standard. Step 1.20 excludes this when $A$ is nonstandard. Thus the socle of every standard has only standard labels. For a simple submodule of a standard-filtered module, choose the first filtration term it intersects nontrivially: it lies in that term, has zero intersection with the preceding term and embeds in the corresponding standard section. Consequently EVERY standard-filtered module has standard-label socle, including all projectives and the tensor object $T$. This is a statement about actual submodules, not about its entire list of composition factors. [F1, F7, step 1.20, step 1.21, construct, algebra]

3.3 The ground central-character multiset determines a unique column-strict label. Within each charge coset its smallest entry $c_\kappa+1-n$ occurs once per column; strictness permits that entry at most once in each column and only at its bottom, so its multiplicity forces every such bottom entry. Remove these entries and repeat with the next minimum in every remaining column. Induction fixes all ground entries. Different charge cosets are distinct and are never compared. In the source convention $\lambda_i=a_i+i-1$, the coordinates $\lambda_i+\rho_i=a_i+(N-1)/2$ show that the central character is precisely this entry multiset. Hence the ground block has the sole column-strict label $A_c$. The generalized standard has diagonal simple multiplicity one and no other simple label in this block, so $N(A_c)=L_O(A_c)$. Actual BGG reciprocity and the projective standard flag give $(P(A_c):N(A_c))=1$ and no other section, so $P_c=P(A_c)=N(A_c)=L_O(A_c)$. Simple-preserving restricted duality makes this simple projective injective. The typed coset equivalence transports the same proof to every admissible complex origin. Tensoring has the exact ordinary-contragredient tensor adjoint on both sides, so $T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ is projective-injective. Simple-preserving restricted transposition duality fixes $P_c$ and the natural module and commutes with this tensor product; hence $T$ is self-dual. Its standard flag follows from the actual parabolic tensor identity, so step 2.4 gives a standard-label socle and duality gives a standard-label head. Conversely every degree-$d$ standard label $A$ is an incoming crystal move $\widetilde f_iB$ from a degree-$d-1$ standard label, except ground in degree zero. Inducting from the ground quotient, exact $f_i$ gives $f_iT_{d-1}\twoheadrightarrow f_iL_O(B)\twoheadrightarrow L_O(A)$ using the ACTUAL simple-head theorem; $f_iT_{d-1}$ is a summand of $T_d$, so $L_O(A)$ is a quotient of $T_d$. Lift any such quotient through its projective cover. Essentiality of the cover makes the lift $T_d\to P(A)$ surjective, and projectivity of $P(A)$ splits it. Therefore the projective summands of $T_d$ are exactly the covers of the standard-label simples, with positive multiplicities; they are injective as summands of $T_d$. It follows that every nonzero submodule $X\subseteq T_d$ has a nonzero standard-label simple socle. Exact $V$ and the nonvanishing already proved in step 1.18 then give $V(X)\ne0$. This proves the required detector; it does not assert that every composition factor of $T_d$ is standard or that $T_d$ generates the whole parabolic category. [F1, F4, F7, step 1.18, step 2.4, construct, algebra]

8.2 $V$ maps $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}$ into $\operatorname{End}_{W}(M)^{\mathrm{op}}=B$ by step 2.5, and its image contains $B$ because every target Hecke operator is the transport of its actual source Casimir/place operator. A nonzero source endomorphism has a nonzero image $X\subseteq T$. Step 3.3 proves $V(X)\ne0$, and exactness identifies $V(X)$ with the image of its transported endomorphism. Hence the endomorphism map is injective as well as surjective, giving $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}=B$. Detection uses the standard-label SOCLE criterion, never a claim that all composition factors of $T$ are standard. [F1, F2, F3, F7, step 7.1, step 3.3, step 2.5, construct, algebra]

9.1 Choose a full finite projective generator Q of the genuine O summand containing T as an explicit summand and write its algebra as A; the projector onto T is e and B=eAe. The exact Schur functor is e(−). It kills precisely the offStd simples. Its left adjoint Ae⊗_B− is right exact and satisfies e(Ae⊗X)=X. The counit Ae⊗eN→N has kernel and cokernel killed by e. Applying V sends it to an isomorphism. Therefore V factors through e(−), and its factor F on B-mod is naturally M⊗_B− by finite free presentations. This factor is exact: the only failure of exactness after the left adjoint is killed by e and hence by Wh. It is faithful, since every B-simple is eL_O(A) for a Std label and its V image is nonzero; exactness then detects every nonzero image of a morphism. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F7, step 1.18, step 3.3, step 8.2, construct, algebra]

Standard/Casimir/Fock interfaces: the highest-weight truncation, the Specht-to-permutation dominance comparison, the Weyl character formula computation, BGG reciprocity and the Fock-basis dictionaries on the source side ([[thm-schur-weyl-decomposition-with-length-cutoff]], [[thm-specht-to-permutation-homomorphism-dominance]], [[thm-weyl-character-formula]], [[thm-bgg-reciprocity]], [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]], [[thm-the-parabolic-o-grothendieck-group-is-the-integral-fock-module]], [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]], [[thm-duflo-joseph-g-finite-endomorphisms-of-verma-modules]], [[def-projective-functors-on-a-regular-integral-category-o-block]], [[prop-base-change-freeness-and-specialization-in-the-deformed-family]], [[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]]).
proof_uses: 1.10 Finite-Levi Weyl gives, on row variables z_(n−q+1),…,z_n, [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]
1.11 ch L(nu)=det(z_r^(nu_s+q−s))/det(z_r^(q−s)) =(Π_(r=n−q+1)^n z_r^(n−1)) det(z_r^(a_s))/det(z_r^(q−s)). [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.12 The numerator exponent is exactly a_s+n−1; the column height and reading offset cancel. The prefactor and denominator are independent of the entries. Products over columns therefore identify the row-torus character of V(N(A)) with a fixed factor times products of nested bottom-row flag minors, evaluated at y_(r,a)=z_r^a. For the ground column a_s=c+1−(n−q+s), the determinant cancels the Vandermonde and gives precisely Π z_r^c, verifying the origin normalization. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.13 All exponential expressions lie in the group algebra of the finitely generated additive subgroup generated by their occurring complex weights and the integral row weights. That subgroup is finitely generated and torsion free, hence free abelian; its group algebra is a Laurent polynomial domain. The nonzero Vandermonde may therefore be cancelled. A zero character of an actual nonzero finite-dimensional module is impossible: its coefficients are nonnegative weight dimensions, and evaluation of the group algebra at1 is its positive dimension. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.14 Fix a finite entry alphabet U, and introduce independent variables y_(r,a), with row space C^n and entry space U. Antisymmetrizing each column of a tensor gives its bottom-row minor, and multiplying gives a GL(U)-linear map from the column-wedge tensor F to Sym(C^n⊗U). Each minor is killed by the lower-row raising operators: replacing a present row by a later row duplicates a row inside its bottom-row set. The product has row weight (p_1,…,p_n). [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.15 Classical Cauchy decomposition follows from the actual published Schur–Weyl decomposition: identify the degree-N symmetric power with diagonal S_N invariants of (C^n)^tensor N⊗U^tensor N, then use the two Specht decompositions. The needed self-duality is complex linear: polytabloids have real coefficients, so their span is conjugation-stable; the bilinear tabloid form B(v,w)=sum v_T w_T is invariant and B(v,conjugate(v)) is the positive Hermitian norm. It is therefore nondegenerate on the Specht span. Schur's lemma with this explicit bilinear duality leaves one multiplicity space for each matching partition. The lower-row highest-weight line at (p_1,…,p_n) selects the partition (p_n,…,p_1), so the entire flag-minor image lies in the irreducible entry module of highest weight Lambda=Σ_j omega_(q_j). The ground product of minors is a nonzero polynomial. Hence the image is exactly this irreducible module. Actual16 proves that this constituent occurs once in F; therefore this nonzero normalized map has exactly the kernel of actual16's highest-component projection pi. No quantum flag algebra or quantum Peter–Weyl theorem is imported. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.16 For different complex cosets, first apply the companion typed category equivalence and use one independent set of variables for each coset. The same Cauchy proof applies to each coset's columns, with their retained sorted heights. Multiplication across the disjoint variable sets is injective on the tensor product. Thus the kernel is the sum of the component projection kernels, exactly the off-standard lower-basis kernel of the product of actual16 models. The shift a↦a−c_kappa+n−n_kappa and inf I_kappa=1−n_kappa is explicit in that companion proof. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.17 V is exact on the genuine parabolic category and sends N(A) to its finite-Levi standard V(A). Actual16 identifies [L_O(A)] with its source positive-parameter dual-canonical vector L_A at parameter1. Its projection pi L_A is zero exactly off Std. The preceding flag-minor factorization consequently gives zero row-torus character of V(L_O(A)) for every off-standard A. Positivity of actual module characters makes V(L_O(A))=0. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.18 The kernel of the Grothendieck map of V is stable under every residue e/f operator, because the actual tensor identity and Casimir/flip compatibility give V e=e V and V f=f Wh. Thus after quotienting by the already-known off-standard kernel, any additional kernel would be a submodule of actual16's irreducible highest component (or the irreducible tensor product for the direct sum of coset root algebras). The ground class survives: its V image is the one-dimensional C_c by the induced-module computation. Hence no additional kernel exists. Every Std simple therefore has a nonzero V image. This argument does not presume that image simple, does not rely on injectivity of the exponential evaluation on the entire abstract polynomial module, and does not require a classification of all finite-dimensional W simples. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.19 Take finite alphabets containing the relevant finite labels and tensor words, with the proved boundary block projections; actual16 gives compatibility under enlarging the cuts. The argument applies on each cut and hence to every object in the selected finite degree/category. All comparisons use integer order within a coset, not an order on C. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

Standard/Casimir/Fock interfaces: the highest-weight truncation, the Specht-to-permutation dominance comparison, the Weyl character formula computation, BGG reciprocity and the Fock-basis dictionaries on the source side ([[thm-schur-weyl-decomposition-with-length-cutoff]], [[thm-specht-to-permutation-homomorphism-dominance]], [[thm-weyl-character-formula]], [[thm-bgg-reciprocity]], [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]], [[thm-the-parabolic-o-grothendieck-group-is-the-integral-fock-module]], [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]], [[thm-duflo-joseph-g-finite-endomorphisms-of-verma-modules]], [[def-projective-functors-on-a-regular-integral-category-o-block]], [[prop-base-change-freeness-and-specialization-in-the-deformed-family]], [[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]]).

1.11 ch L(nu)=det(z_r^(nu_s+q−s))/det(z_r^(q−s)) =(Π_(r=n−q+1)^n z_r^(n−1)) det(z_r^(a_s))/det(z_r^(q−s)). [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.12 The numerator exponent is exactly a_s+n−1; the column height and reading offset cancel. The prefactor and denominator are independent of the entries. Products over columns therefore identify the row-torus character of V(N(A)) with a fixed factor times products of nested bottom-row flag minors, evaluated at y_(r,a)=z_r^a. For the ground column a_s=c+1−(n−q+s), the determinant cancels the Vandermonde and gives precisely Π z_r^c, verifying the origin normalization. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.13 All exponential expressions lie in the group algebra of the finitely generated additive subgroup generated by their occurring complex weights and the integral row weights. That subgroup is finitely generated and torsion free, hence free abelian; its group algebra is a Laurent polynomial domain. The nonzero Vandermonde may therefore be cancelled. A zero character of an actual nonzero finite-dimensional module is impossible: its coefficients are nonnegative weight dimensions, and evaluation of the group algebra at1 is its positive dimension. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.14 Fix a finite entry alphabet U, and introduce independent variables y_(r,a), with row space C^n and entry space U. Antisymmetrizing each column of a tensor gives its bottom-row minor, and multiplying gives a GL(U)-linear map from the column-wedge tensor F to Sym(C^n⊗U). Each minor is killed by the lower-row raising operators: replacing a present row by a later row duplicates a row inside its bottom-row set. The product has row weight (p_1,…,p_n). [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.15 Classical Cauchy decomposition follows from the actual published Schur–Weyl decomposition: identify the degree-N symmetric power with diagonal S_N invariants of (C^n)^tensor N⊗U^tensor N, then use the two Specht decompositions. The needed self-duality is complex linear: polytabloids have real coefficients, so their span is conjugation-stable; the bilinear tabloid form B(v,w)=sum v_T w_T is invariant and B(v,conjugate(v)) is the positive Hermitian norm. It is therefore nondegenerate on the Specht span. Schur's lemma with this explicit bilinear duality leaves one multiplicity space for each matching partition. The lower-row highest-weight line at (p_1,…,p_n) selects the partition (p_n,…,p_1), so the entire flag-minor image lies in the irreducible entry module of highest weight Lambda=Σ_j omega_(q_j). The ground product of minors is a nonzero polynomial. Hence the image is exactly this irreducible module. Actual16 proves that this constituent occurs once in F; therefore this nonzero normalized map has exactly the kernel of actual16's highest-component projection pi. No quantum flag algebra or quantum Peter–Weyl theorem is imported. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.16 For different complex cosets, first apply the companion typed category equivalence and use one independent set of variables for each coset. The same Cauchy proof applies to each coset's columns, with their retained sorted heights. Multiplication across the disjoint variable sets is injective on the tensor product. Thus the kernel is the sum of the component projection kernels, exactly the off-standard lower-basis kernel of the product of actual16 models. The shift a↦a−c_kappa+n−n_kappa and inf I_kappa=1−n_kappa is explicit in that companion proof. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.17 V is exact on the genuine parabolic category and sends N(A) to its finite-Levi standard V(A). Actual16 identifies [L_O(A)] with its source positive-parameter dual-canonical vector L_A at parameter1. Its projection pi L_A is zero exactly off Std. The preceding flag-minor factorization consequently gives zero row-torus character of V(L_O(A)) for every off-standard A. Positivity of actual module characters makes V(L_O(A))=0. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.18 The kernel of the Grothendieck map of V is stable under every residue e/f operator, because the actual tensor identity and Casimir/flip compatibility give V e=e V and V f=f Wh. Thus after quotienting by the already-known off-standard kernel, any additional kernel would be a submodule of actual16's irreducible highest component (or the irreducible tensor product for the direct sum of coset root algebras). The ground class survives: its V image is the one-dimensional C_c by the induced-module computation. Hence no additional kernel exists. Every Std simple therefore has a nonzero V image. This argument does not presume that image simple, does not rely on injectivity of the exponential evaluation on the entire abstract polynomial module, and does not require a classification of all finite-dimensional W simples. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.19 Take finite alphabets containing the relevant finite labels and tensor words, with the proved boundary block projections; actual16 gives compatibility under enlarging the cuts. The argument applies on each cut and hence to every object in the selected finite degree/category. All comparisons use integer order within a coset, not an order on C. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.20 The actual highest-component projection $\pi$ is module-linear and, in its integral $L/D$ bases, is the coordinate projection with $\pi L_A=0$ off $\mathrm{Std}$ and $\pi L_A=D_A$ on $\mathrm{Std}$. Its kernel is therefore a direct summand, and specialization at parameter one gives exactly $K=\bigoplus_{A\notin\mathrm{Std}}\mathbb Z L_A(1)$, with no extra specialization kernel. For a nonstandard simple, exact residue translation and the source $K_0$ dictionary give $[f_iL_O(A)]\in K$ and $[e_iL_O(A)]\in K$. Expanding these actual modules in their simple classes and projecting gives a sum of independent $D_B(1)$ with nonnegative composition multiplicities; each standard-label coefficient must vanish. Exactness then proves that the Serre subcategory of objects with only off-standard composition factors is stable under both residue functors. In several complex cosets apply the product of component coordinate projections and the typed residue shift $i^{\mathrm{int}}=i-c_\kappa+n-n_\kappa$. To treat finitely many objects or elementary moves outside an initial admitted cut, shift every origin down by a sufficiently large common integer; the category, cosets and standard predicate are unchanged and all those labels lie above the new ground. No order on different complex cosets is used. [F1, F4, F7, construct, algebra]

1.21 Every standard $N(C)$ embeds in an iterated lowering translate of a standard simple. To construct the monomorphism, shift the entries of column $j$ upwards by an integer $k_j\ge0$, choosing these successively so that every shifted entry in that column is greater than every earlier-column entry in the same coset. The resulting $B$ is standard and minimal in its fixed-multiset Bruhat orbit; the triangular standard/simple multiplicity matrix gives $N(B)=L_O(B)$. For each column $j=2,\ldots,l$, list its original entries increasingly and lower its smallest entry from $a+k_j$ to $a$, then its next entry, and so on, using $e_{a+k_j-1},\ldots,e_a$ in that chronological order. At each step the distinguished change in column $j$ is valid: its smaller entries already have their original values, while its larger entries and the later columns remain above the required range. Every other valid change occurs in an earlier column and gives a strictly smaller label in the prefix Bruhat order. The distinguished standard is therefore the largest section of the multiplicity-free residue standard flag. Move it to the bottom by splitting adjacent extensions. Indeed the projective-cover kernel of $N(D)$ is filtered by standards $N(E)$ with $E>D$, while $\operatorname{Hom}(N(E),N(C))=0$ unless $E\le C$, since a nonzero image has its $L_O(E)$ head as a composition factor of $N(C)$. Thus for largest $D$ and smaller $C$, every map from that projective kernel to $N(C)$ vanishes; the projective-cover exact sequence gives $\operatorname{Ext}^1(N(D),N(C))=0$. This proves the precise splitting orientation locally from the highest-weight suppliers. This produces an actual monomorphism at each elementary step. Exactness preserves these monomorphisms under the remaining lowering functors, giving $N(C)\hookrightarrow e_{i_1}\cdots e_{i_r}L_O(B)$. For mixed cosets the same construction is performed only among comparable entries; the typed standard and tensor equivalence transports the inclusion. [F1, F4, F7, construct, algebra]

3.3 The ground central-character multiset determines a unique column-strict label. Within each charge coset its smallest entry $c_\kappa+1-n$ occurs once per column; strictness permits that entry at most once in each column and only at its bottom, so its multiplicity forces every such bottom entry. Remove these entries and repeat with the next minimum in every remaining column. Induction fixes all ground entries. Different charge cosets are distinct and are never compared. In the source convention $\lambda_i=a_i+i-1$, the coordinates $\lambda_i+\rho_i=a_i+(N-1)/2$ show that the central character is precisely this entry multiset. Hence the ground block has the sole column-strict label $A_c$. The generalized standard has diagonal simple multiplicity one and no other simple label in this block, so $N(A_c)=L_O(A_c)$. Actual BGG reciprocity and the projective standard flag give $(P(A_c):N(A_c))=1$ and no other section, so $P_c=P(A_c)=N(A_c)=L_O(A_c)$. Simple-preserving restricted duality makes this simple projective injective. The typed coset equivalence transports the same proof to every admissible complex origin. Tensoring has the exact ordinary-contragredient tensor adjoint on both sides, so $T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ is projective-injective. Simple-preserving restricted transposition duality fixes $P_c$ and the natural module and commutes with this tensor product; hence $T$ is self-dual. Its standard flag follows from the actual parabolic tensor identity, so step 2.4 gives a standard-label socle and duality gives a standard-label head. Conversely every degree-$d$ standard label $A$ is an incoming crystal move $\widetilde f_iB$ from a degree-$d-1$ standard label, except ground in degree zero. Inducting from the ground quotient, exact $f_i$ gives $f_iT_{d-1}\twoheadrightarrow f_iL_O(B)\twoheadrightarrow L_O(A)$ using the ACTUAL simple-head theorem; $f_iT_{d-1}$ is a summand of $T_d$, so $L_O(A)$ is a quotient of $T_d$. Lift any such quotient through its projective cover. Essentiality of the cover makes the lift $T_d\to P(A)$ surjective, and projectivity of $P(A)$ splits it. Therefore the projective summands of $T_d$ are exactly the covers of the standard-label simples, with positive multiplicities; they are injective as summands of $T_d$. It follows that every nonzero submodule $X\subseteq T_d$ has a nonzero standard-label simple socle. Exact $V$ and the nonvanishing already proved in step 1.18 then give $V(X)\ne0$. This proves the required detector; it does not assert that every composition factor of $T_d$ is standard or that $T_d$ generates the whole parabolic category. [F1, F4, F7, step 1.18, step 2.4, construct, algebra]

4.2 Fix an admissible origin: c_j−c_k integral implies c_j=c_k. The original arbitrary-origin deformed tensor algebra remains separate and unrestricted. In a column of height q whose global row numbers are n−q+1,…,n, write its strict entries a_1,…,a_q. The genuine head-model action proved in step 3.1 makes its finite-Levi highest weight nu_s=a_s+n−q+s−1. This follows directly from the global highest weight lambda_i=a_i+i−1 and eta_head diagonal shift n−q_1−…−q_col: the column-reading position i=q_before+(global_row−n+q) gives lambda_i+eta_head=a_i+global_row−1. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

7.1 Fix the head-normalized ground map $i_0:V(P_c)\to\mathbb C_c$ obtained from step 3.1 and the finite-Levi character calculation below. Iterate $\nu$ on $P_c\otimes V^{\otimes(d-1)}$ to obtain $i_d:V(P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d})\to\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}$, and compose with the proved ACTUAL balanced tensor map $\mu_d$ to get $j_d$. Casimir and flip compatibility prove $(W,H_d)$-bimodule linearity. Any source endomorphism $b$ is transported as $j_dV(b)j_d^{-1}$; in particular a native Casimir/place word representing right multiplication by $h$ becomes the actual map $m\mapsto mh$. This identifies maps in the cyclotomic IMAGE algebra, without asserting a faithful abstract Hecke action outside its allowed range. The construction uses no origin integrality. Typed category-O/coset transport is used only for the selected admissible-origin source labels and their character dictionaries, whereas the unrestricted deformed tensor model retains its arbitrary origins. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 3.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, construct, algebra]

8.1 $H_d$ acts on $T$ by the universal tensor Casimir and places. At the first tensor step the actual finite $\mathfrak p$ flag of the natural module has one standard section per column. On the $j$th section, the ordinary quadratic-Casimir identity $\Omega=(C_{\mathrm{total}}-C_{\mathrm{source}}-C_V)/2$ gives eigenvalue $c_j+q_j-n$. Successively applying the factors in the column-order flag makes $\prod_j(x_1-(c_j+q_j-n))$ annihilate $T$; subsequent tensor factors leave this first-step relation intact. Hence the source action factors through the genuine cyclotomic algebra, not only its $V$ image. Step 7.1 transports it to $M=V_c^{\otimes d}$ as the actual $(W,H_d)$ bimodule action. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 6.1, step 7.1, construct, algebra]

9.1 Choose a full finite projective generator Q of the genuine O summand containing T as an explicit summand and write its algebra as A; the projector onto T is e and B=eAe. The exact Schur functor is e(−). It kills precisely the offStd simples. Its left adjoint Ae⊗_B− is right exact and satisfies e(Ae⊗X)=X. The counit Ae⊗eN→N has kernel and cokernel killed by e. Applying V sends it to an isomorphism. Therefore V factors through e(−), and its factor F on B-mod is naturally M⊗_B− by finite free presentations. This factor is exact: the only failure of exactness after the left adjoint is killed by e and hence by Wh. It is faithful, since every B-simple is eL_O(A) for a Std label and its V image is nonzero; exactness then detects every nonzero image of a morphism. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F7, step 1.18, step 3.3, step 8.2, construct, algebra]

10.1 A finite-dimensional right B-module whose tensor functor is exact is projective. Explicitly, take its finite projective cover P→M with kernel K⊂P rad B. Tensor the inclusion K→P with B/rad B; flatness makes K/K rad B inject into P/P rad B, but this map is zero, so Nakayama gives K=0. Faithfulness forces every right indecomposable projective to occur in M: otherwise tensor with the corresponding left simple would vanish. Thus M_B is a progenerator. The first independently proved raw centralizer identity in step 2.5 gives Wd=End_B(M). The usual generator presentation/evaluation argument now gives the genuine Morita equivalence Wd-mod≃B-mod. In particular F sends B-simples to Wd-simples, proving the full relevant V simple-image claim without assuming it earlier. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F8, step 2.5, step 9.1, construct, algebra]

11.1 Tensor compatibility and the actual Casimir/flip intertwiners are proved in steps 1.9–1.18, using the original head/right normalizer and the actual balanced Skryabin map. Thus $V(P_c)=\mathbb C_c$ and $V(P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d})=V_c^{\otimes d}$. The preceding kernel/Morita construction proves $V(L_{\mathcal O}(A))=L_W(A)$ for standard labels and zero otherwise; it never asserts that the image of a source standard $N(A)$ is simple. The normalized comparison is determined on the ground and its tensor words, hence on the detecting tensor bimodule and on finite free quotient presentations through the established exact Morita factorization. Its ground normalization removes scalar ambiguity. This proves the stated properties of the genuine Whittaker functor, while keeping it distinct from the Hecke Hom quotient. [F1, F2, F3, F4, choose, construct, algebra] ∎

rows.consumer_statement_or_definition:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the angular Lebesgue
measure clause below; under it $\lambda_1$ is a measure and intervals have
their usual lengths ([[thm-lebesgue-measure-is-a-complete-measure]],
[[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]]).

Let $\mathbb T:=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ be the multiplicative unit circle
with its subspace topology from $\mathbb C$
([[lem-unit-circle-is-a-compact-metrizable-topological-group]]), identified
with angular frequencies by $z=e^{i\lambda}$. Write $d\lambda$ for
the finite angular Lebesgue Borel measure obtained from ordinary Lebesgue
measure on $[-\pi,\pi)$; thus $d\lambda(\mathbb T)=2\pi$, and the endpoints
$-\pi$ and $\pi$ denote the same point. The characters of discrete additive
$\mathbb Z$ are $h\mapsto e^{ih\lambda}$ by
[[thm-discrete-integers-have-circle-dual]].

For angular representatives $\lambda,\theta\in\mathbb R$, define their
circular distance by
$$d_{\mathbb T}(\lambda,\theta):=\min_{k\in\mathbb Z}|\lambda-\theta+2\pi k|.$$
The minimum exists because the displayed absolute values tend to infinity
with $|k|$, and changing either representative by $2\pi$ leaves it unchanged.

Precisely, for Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb T$ put
$$d\lambda(B):=\lambda_1\{\theta\in[-\pi,\pi):e^{i\theta}\in B\}.$$
The map $\theta\mapsto e^{i\theta}$ is continuous by
[[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]] and
[[cor-complex-differentiability-implies-continuity]], so the preimage is
Borel by [[thm-continuous-preimages-of-borel-sets-are-borel]]. Preimages
preserve disjoint unions, so this is a finite Borel measure under the stated
Countable Choice premise. Integrating a Borel function of the circle angle
means integrating its periodic lift over this half-open interval.

Let $X=(X_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ be a real weakly stationary process with mean
$\mu$ and autocovariance $\gamma(h)=\operatorname{Cov}(X_{t+h},X_t)$
([[def-strict-and-weak-stationarity-for-time-series]],
[[def-autocovariance-and-sample-autocovariance]]). A **spectral measure** for
$X$ is a finite positive Radon Borel measure $F$ on $\mathbb T$
([[def-radon-measure-on-an-lch-space]]) satisfying
$$\gamma(h)=\int_{\mathbb T}e^{ih\lambda}\,F(d\lambda)\qquad(h\in\mathbb Z).$$
Putting $h=0$ gives $F(\mathbb T)=\gamma(0)$. A **spectral density** is a
nonnegative measurable function $f$ with
$$F(B)=\int_B f(\lambda)\,d\lambda$$
for every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb T$; it exists only when $F$ is
absolutely continuous with respect to $d\lambda$ and is unique up to
$d\lambda$-null sets.

For a known mean $\mu$ and integer $n\ge1$, the **known-mean periodogram** is
the random function
$$I_n(\lambda):=\frac1{2\pi n}\left|\sum_{t=1}^n(X_t-\mu)e^{-it\lambda}\right|^2,\qquad\lambda\in\mathbb T.$$
The centering uses the population mean, not the sample mean. The finite sum is
square-integrable, so $I_n(\lambda)$ has finite expectation: for
$Y_t=X_t-\mu$, the pointwise inequality
$|\sum_{t=1}^nY_te^{-it\lambda}|^2\le n\sum_{t=1}^n|Y_t|^2$ bounds its
expectation by $n\sum_{t=1}^n\mathbb E[Y_t^2]<\infty$
([[def-moments-variance-and-covariance]]).

Define the normalized finite-sample Fejér kernel
$$\Phi_n(x):=\frac1{2\pi n}\left|\sum_{t=1}^ne^{-itx}\right|^2,\qquad x\in\mathbb T.$$

For smoothing, let $K:\mathbb R\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous with compact
support, $\int_{\mathbb R}K(u)\,du=1$, and $K(0)>0$. For bandwidth $b>0$,
periodize it on the circle by
$$K_b(x):=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}\frac1bK\!\left(\frac{x+2\pi k}{b}\right).$$
Compact support makes this a finite sum at each $x$, and changing variables
over the intervals that tile $\mathbb R$ gives
$\int_{\mathbb T}K_b(x)\,d\lambda(x)=1$. Fix a sequence of bandwidths
$(b_n)_{n\ge1}$ with $b_n>0$. For the Fourier grid
$\lambda_{j,n}=2\pi j/n$ ($0\le j<n$) and target $\lambda_0\in\mathbb T$, when
the denominator is positive define
$$w_{n,j}(\lambda_0):=\frac{K_{b_n}(\lambda_0-\lambda_{j,n})}{\sum_{\ell=0}^{n-1}K_{b_n}(\lambda_0-\lambda_{\ell,n})},\qquad \widetilde f_n(\lambda_0):=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}w_{n,j}(\lambda_0)I_n(\lambda_{j,n}).$$
The weights are nonnegative and sum to one.

rows.consumer_statement_or_definition:
Fix a reduced complex-analytic plane curve germ $X$ at a point
$p\in\mathbb C^2$, that is, a hypersurface germ in $\mathbb C^2$ given by an
equation whose square-free reduction is itself
([[def-complex-analytic-hypersurface-germ-and-reduced-equation]]). Write
$I_p(X)$ for its vanishing ideal and define the **local ring of the curve
germ**

$$A:=\mathcal O_{\mathbb C^2,p}/I_p(X).$$

By the principal vanishing-ideal lemma, choosing a reduced defining equation
$f$ of $X$ gives $I_p(X)=(f)$ and hence
$A=\mathcal O_{\mathbb C^2,p}/(f)$; in particular $A$ is the same ring for
every reduced defining equation of $X$
([[lem-vanishing-ideal-of-a-reduced-hypersurface-germ]]).

Let

$$S:=\{a\in A:\ a\ \text{is a nonzerodivisor of }A\}$$

be the set of nonzerodivisors. Then $S$ is a multiplicative subset of $A$
([[def-multiplicative-subset-and-localisation]]): $1\in S$, and if $s,t\in S$
and $st\,x=0$ for some $x\in A$, then $t(sx)=0$, so $sx=0$ because $t$ is a
nonzerodivisor and then $x=0$ because $s$ is one; thus $st\in S$.

The **total quotient ring** of the curve germ is the localisation

$$Q(A):=S^{-1}A,$$

with its localisation map $A\to Q(A)$, $a\mapsto a/1$. Since $S$ consists of
the nonzerodivisors, this map is injective and every nonzerodivisor of $A$
becomes a unit in $Q(A)$; the ring $Q(A)$ is the largest localisation of $A$ in
which the map is injective.

The **normalisation** of $A$ is the integral closure of $A$ in $Q(A)$: the set
of elements of $Q(A)$ that are integral over $A$, i.e. roots of monic
polynomials with coefficients in the image of $A$
([[def-integral-element-and-algebraic-integer]],
[[def-integral-closure-and-integrally-closed-domain]]). Explicitly, writing
the localisation map as an inclusion,

$$\overline A=\{b\in Q(A):\ b^k+a_1b^{k-1}+\cdots+a_k=0\ \text{for some }k\ge1\ \text{and }a_i\in A\}.$$

The curve germ $X$ is **normal** when $A=\overline A$, that is, when $A$ is
integrally closed in $Q(A)$.

rows.consumer_statement_or_definition:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Work in category
$\mathcal O$ with the conventions of the preceding definitions. For a weight
$\lambda$ write $\chi_\lambda$ for the generalized central character obtained
from $\lambda$, so that $\chi_\lambda=\chi_\mu$ if and only if
$\mu\in W\mathbin\cdot\lambda$
([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]), and let
$\mathcal O=\bigoplus_\chi\mathcal O_\chi$ be the central-character
decomposition of [[thm-category-o-decomposes-by-generalized-central-character]]
with inclusions $\operatorname{incl}_\chi$ and exact projections
$\operatorname{pr}_\chi$, so that
$\operatorname{pr}_\chi\circ\operatorname{incl}_\chi=\operatorname{id}$.

For a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-module $E$
([[def-weight-and-weight-space-of-a-lie-algebra-representation]]) and two
generalized central characters $\chi,\chi'$, set
$$T_{\chi,E,\chi'}:=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi'}\circ(E\otimes-)\circ\operatorname{incl}_\chi\colon\mathcal O_\chi\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\chi'}.$$
This is well defined because $E\otimes-$ is an exact endofunctor of
$\mathcal O$
([[prop-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-category-o]])
and the projections and inclusions are exact.

For weights $\lambda,\mu$ with $\mu-\lambda$ integral
([[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]]), let $\nu$ be the

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a finite-dimensional
complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$,
and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$ with the
conventions of [[def-bgg-category-o]]: positive roots $\Phi^+$, simple roots
$\alpha_i$, $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$, the root order $\mu\le\lambda$
meaning $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, Weyl vector $\rho$, the dot action
$w\mathbin\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$, and category
$\mathcal O$.

For a weight $\lambda$ let $C=W_\lambda\mathbin\cdot\lambda$ be its
integral-reflection linkage class in the sense of
[[def-integral-weyl-group-of-a-weight]]; it is contained in the full dot orbit
$W\mathbin\cdot\lambda$, hence finite because $W$ is finite
([[prop-the-weyl-group-is-finite-and-acts-faithfully-on-the-root-system]],
with the identification of the abstract reflections with the $s_\alpha$ of
[[prop-the-roots-form-a-reduced-crystallographic-euclidean-root-system]]).
A **finite downward-closed ideal** of $C$ is a finite subset $\Gamma\subseteq C$
such that
$$\nu\in\Gamma\ \text{and}\ \mu\in C\ \text{and}\ \mu\le\nu\ \Longrightarrow\ \mu\in\Gamma ,$$
where $\le$ is the root order of [[def-bgg-category-o]] and not the strong
linkage order $\uparrow$ of [[def-strong-linkage-order-on-weights]]. It is a
lower set in the restriction of the partial order $\le$ to $C$. The empty
ideal is allowed; every nonempty such ideal has minimal elements.

For such a $\Gamma$, the **truncation** $\mathcal O_\Gamma$ is the full
subcategory of $\mathcal O$ whose objects are those $X$ all of whose simple
composition factors are $L(\mu)$ with $\mu\in\Gamma$; composition factors are
those of [[def-composition-series-and-composition-factors-of-an-object]] and
the simple objects of $\mathcal O$ are the $L(\mu)$ of
[[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]]. Because every
object of $\mathcal O$ has finite length
([[thm-every-category-o-object-has-finite-length]]) and composition factors of
a composition series are independent of the chosen series
([[thm-jordan-holder-theorem-in-an-abelian-category]]), membership in
$\mathcal O_\Gamma$ depends only on the isomorphism class of the object and
not on a chosen composition series. Consequently $\mathcal O_\Gamma$ contains
the zero object and is closed in $\mathcal O$ under finite direct sums,
subobjects, quotients and extensions
([[thm-category-o-is-abelian-and-extension-closed]]); it is the truncation of
the finite label poset of one linkage class.

The Verma-placement claim below also has a direct justification. The highest weight line of $M(\mu)$ is one-dimensional and generates the whole module; hence it cannot be distributed among two nonzero direct summands. The linkage-block decomposition of [[thm-central-character-summands-split-into-linkage-blocks]] therefore places this Verma in the block of its unique simple quotient $L(\mu)$ ([[thm-verma-module-has-a-unique-simple-quotient]]), so all its composition labels lie in $C$. A label $\eta$ of a composition factor is a weight of $M(\mu)$: in a short exact sequence of $\mathfrak h$-semisimple modules, a weight vector in the quotient lifts in that same weight by extracting that component of any finite weight decomposition of a lift. Iterating through a composition series and using [[prop-weights-of-a-verma-module-lie-below-lambda]] gives $\eta\le\mu$. Thus $\mu\in\Gamma$ and lower closure within $C$ force every such $\eta\in\Gamma$, proving $M(\mu)\in\mathcal O_\Gamma$ without a bound by one greatest label.

Two boundaries are part of the definition. First, $\mathcal O_\Gamma$ is a
condition on the highest-weight labels of simple composition factors, not a
bound on all weights of a Verma module: a Verma module $M(\mu)$ with
$\mu\in\Gamma$ lies in $\mathcal O_\Gamma$ although its weights run over the
whole cone $\mu-Q^+$. Second, $\Gamma$ is a finite ideal inside a single
linkage class $C$, not the infinite lower ideal generated by $\lambda$ in the
whole weight lattice; in particular a discrete series truncation is a
different construction.

Let $H$ be a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space and let $M\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ be a concrete factor von Neumann algebra ([[def-factor-representation-and-primary-representation]]). A nonzero projection $p\in M$ is **minimal**, or **abelian**, when $pMp=\mathbb Cp$. The factor $M$ is of **type I** when it contains a nonzero minimal projection. A strongly continuous unitary representation $\pi$ of a topological group $G$ on a nonzero separable Hilbert space is a **type I factor representation** when its generated von Neumann algebra $\pi(G)''$ is a factor of type I; and a factor representation is of type I when it is a multiple of an irreducible representation (equivalently, by [[lem-separable-type-i-factors-are-multiples-of-irreducible-representations]], when $\pi(G)''$ contains a nonzero minimal projection). The group $G$ is **type I** when every factor representation of $G$ on a separable Hilbert space is of type I. The two descriptions of a type I factor representation agree: for a strongly continuous unitary representation $\pi$ on nonzero separable $H$ with $M=\pi(G)''$ a factor, $M$ contains a nonzero minimal projection if and only if there is an irreducible representation $\sigma$ of $G$ and $m\in\{1,2,\dots,\infty\}$ with $\pi\cong\sigma^{\oplus m}$ ([[lem-separable-type-i-factors-are-multiples-of-irreducible-representations]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff topological group. Two strongly continuous unitary representations $\pi$ on $H$ and $\sigma$ on $H'$ of $K$ are **unitarily equivalent** when there is a unitary intertwiner between them, that is, a bijective linear isometry $U:H\to H'$ with $U\pi(k)=\sigma(k)U$ for every $k\in K$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]]). The **unitary dual** (dual object) $\widehat K$ is the set of unitary equivalence classes of irreducible strongly continuous unitary representations of $K$.

By [[thm-continuous-irreducible-unitary-representations-of-compact-groups-are-finite-dimensional]], under the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) every irreducible strongly continuous unitary representation of $K$ has finite-dimensional carrier: the carrier admits an ordered basis of finite length $d$, its dimension $d_\pi:=\dim_{\mathbb C}H_\pi\ge1$ ([[def-dimension]]), and every class contains a representative whose carrier is $\mathbb C^d$ ([[cor-finite-dimensional-inner-product-spaces-have-orthonormal-bases]] realizes the carrier as $\mathbb C^d$ through an orthonormal basis). Consequently $\widehat K$ is a set: it is the union over $d\ge1$ of the set of unitary equivalence classes of irreducible representations on the fixed carrier $\mathbb C^d$, and equivalence on a fixed carrier is a relation on the set of group homomorphisms $K\to U(d)$.

**Standing conventions.** When a statement uses a representative $\pi$ of a class in $\widehat K$, or an orthonormal basis of its carrier, such choices are licensed by the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and every assertion made this way must be invariant under unitary equivalence; the normalized coefficient family of [[def-normalized-irreducible-matrix-coefficient-basis]] is the first instance. Irreducibility is understood in the sense of [[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]], so every class in $\widehat K$ has nonzero carrier and $d_\pi\ge1$. No topology is placed on $\widehat K$ and no countability of $\widehat K$ is asserted.

Let $X$ be a connected Riemann surface
([[def-riemann-surface-and-holomorphic-atlas]]); assume the Axiom of Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) throughout.

**The holomorphic universal cover.** A **universal covering space** of $X$ is a
covering map $p:\widetilde X\to X$ with $\widetilde X$ simply connected
([[def-universal-covering-space]],
[[def-covering-map-and-evenly-covered-neighbourhoods]],
[[def-simply-connected]]).

*Existence.* A Riemann surface is a topological $2$-manifold without boundary,
hence locally compact and locally path connected, and every point has a
neighbourhood basis of path-connected open sets
([[prop-topological-manifolds-are-locally-compact-and-locally-path-connected]]);
being connected and locally path connected, $X$ is path connected
([[thm-connected-and-locally-path-connected-implies-path-connected]]). It is
semilocally simply connected in the sense of
[[def-semilocally-simply-connected-space]]: given $x\in X$ and a chart whose
image is an open disc, the chart domain $U$ is homeomorphic to a disc, a
nonempty convex subset of $\mathbb R^2$, hence simply connected
([[thm-convex-subsets-have-trivial-fundamental-group]]), so every loop in $U$
is null in $U$, therefore null in $X$, and the inclusion induces the trivial
map on fundamental groups. The existence theorem
([[thm-universal-cover-existence]]) therefore supplies at least one universal
covering space $p:\widetilde X\to X$.

*Holomorphic structure.* By
[[lem-holomorphic-structure-lifts-to-covering-surface]] (which uses Countable
Choice, a consequence of the Axiom of Choice) the topological universal cover
carries a complex structure, unique for which the projection is a holomorphic
unbranched covering, and with it $\widetilde X$ is a second-countable Riemann
surface and every deck transformation is biholomorphic. **The holomorphic
universal cover** of $X$ means $\widetilde X$ with this structure.

**The type.** The simply connected Riemann surface $\widetilde X$ is
biholomorphic to exactly one of the Riemann sphere $\widehat{\mathbb C}$, the
complex plane $\mathbb C$ and the unit disc $\mathbb D$
([[thm-uniformization-simply-connected-riemann-surfaces]]). Accordingly $X$ is

- **spherical** when its holomorphic universal cover is biholomorphic to
  $\widehat{\mathbb C}$,
- **parabolic** when its holomorphic universal cover is biholomorphic to
  $\mathbb C$,
- **hyperbolic** when its holomorphic universal cover is biholomorphic to
  $\mathbb D$.

**Well-definedness.** The label is independent of the universal cover chosen.
Let $p:\widetilde X\to X$ and $q:\widetilde Y\to X$ be two universal covers and
fix basepoints over the same point of $X$. By
[[thm-universal-cover-uniqueness-and-dominating-property]] there is a unique
continuous map $\varphi:\widetilde X\to\widetilde Y$ over $X$ (that is,
$q\circ\varphi=p$), and it is a homeomorphism, since the same statement applied
with the roles exchanged produces its inverse. The lifted complex structures of
[[lem-holomorphic-structure-lifts-to-covering-surface]] make $p$ and $q$
holomorphic unbranched coverings, hence local biholomorphisms; on a small open
set of $\widetilde X$ on which $q$ is injective the map $\varphi$ equals the
composite of $p$ with the holomorphic local inverse of $q$, so $\varphi$ is
holomorphic, and symmetrically for $\varphi^{-1}$. Thus $\varphi$ is a
biholomorphism ([[def-biholomorphic-map]]), the two universal covers are
biholomorphic, and they determine the same one of the three models. Exactly one
label occurs, for two reasons: the uniformization theorem presents $X$'s cover
as one of the three models, and no two of the three are biholomorphic
([[lem-three-simply-connected-models-are-inequivalent]]), so two labels cannot
both apply. The three labels are therefore exhaustive and mutually exclusive
for connected Riemann surfaces.

rows.consumer_statement_or_definition:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Work in category
$\mathcal O$ with the conventions of [[def-bgg-category-o]], and write
$\Delta(\mu)=M(\mu)$ for the standard objects of
[[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]], i.e. the Verma modules
of [[def-verma-module]].

A **finite Verma flag** of an object $X$ of $\mathcal O$ — also called a
**standard flag** or a **$\Delta$-flag** — is a finite increasing sequence of
subobjects
$$0=X_0\subseteq X_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq X_n=X$$
such that each quotient $X_i/X_{i-1}$ is isomorphic to a Verma module
$\Delta(\mu_i)=M(\mu_i)$, for $i=1,\dots,n$. An object admitting such a flag is
called **Verma-filtered**. Since the flag is exhausted by its factors, its
class in the Grothendieck group
$K_0(\mathcal O)$ of [[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]]
is
$$[X]=\sum_{i=1}^n[\Delta(\mu_i)].$$

For a Verma-filtered object $X$ and a weight $\mu$, the **multiplicity**
$(X:\Delta(\mu))$ is the number of indices $i$ with $\mu_i=\mu$ in a Verma
flag of $X$. This number is independent of the chosen flag by
[[lem-verma-flag-multiplicities-are-independent-of-the-flag]], so the notation
$(X:\Delta(\mu))$ is well-defined for Verma-filtered $X$.

The zero object has the empty flag, and every multiplicity of the zero object
is zero; a nonzero Verma-filtered object has at least one factor. A one-step
flag of $X$ is exactly an isomorphism $X\cong\Delta(\mu)$ for a single weight
$\mu$, so the objects with a one-step flag are the Verma modules themselves.
The flag is a chain of subobjects of $X$ in the module category; it is not
required to split, and later examples show that it need not.

rows.consumer_statement_or_definition:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $M$ be an object of the category $\mathcal O$ of [[def-bgg-category-o]]. A **Verma filtration** of $M$ is a finite increasing filtration by $\mathfrak g$-submodules

$$0=M_0\subseteq M_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq M_n=M$$

such that for every $j$ there is a weight $\psi_j$ with $M_j/M_{j-1}\cong M(\psi_j)$, the Verma module of [[def-verma-module]]. When such a filtration exists, $M$ is called **Verma-filtered** and one writes

$$\operatorname{Typ}M=\{\psi_1,\dots,\psi_n\},$$

a finite multiset of weights, its **type**. The multiset is independent of the chosen filtration: passing to classes in the Grothendieck group of [[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]] gives $[M]=\sum_j[M(\psi_j)]$, and by [[prop-the-grothendieck-group-of-o-has-simple-and-standard-bases]] the classes of the Verma modules involved have pairwise distinct characters and are linearly independent in the relevant block, so the multiset of weights is recovered from $[M]$. Consequently $\operatorname{Typ}$ is well defined. The standard example is a finite direct sum $M=\bigoplus_{r=1}^{n}M(\psi_r)$, which is Verma-filtered with type $\{\psi_1,\dots,\psi_n\}$ by taking the partial sums of the summands. Verma-filteredness is also preserved by tensoring with a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module: [[prop-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-category-o]] keeps the module in $\mathcal O$, and the type of the tensor product is computed by the page's tensoring lemma.
